rules.note: Compiler extensions: __attribute__, __declspec, __asm, __builtin_*, __int128, typeof...
Unions are reported (use std::variant).
Non-const variables at namespace scope, and const pointers to non-const data.
void* parameters or returns, and more than one bool parameter.
Only with cpp20Guidelines.gsl.enabled: a pointer parameter checked against nullptr (or asserted) on entry.
Reports functions with more than cpp20Guidelines.thresholds.maxParameters (default 6: the guideline calls 7 or more suspicious).
Limits come from the guideline text: 60 lines, 140 columns, 10 logical paths (a switch counts as one). All configurable.
Named parameters that are never used in the function (a parameter marked [[maybe_unused]] is accepted).
Cheap builtin/view types passed by reference to const, std::array above 4 pointers by value, and moved references; class sizes are not known.
X&& parameters (X not a template parameter) that are never passed to std::move.
Forwarding references that are used other than as std::forward<T>(x), or forwarded twice on one path.
std::pair / std::tuple return types (variadic templates are exempt).
A pointer parameter followed by an integral parameter that is count-named, or whose body indexes the pointer and bounds a loop by the count.
Returning &local, a local array, or a local by reference.
main must return int.
Assignment operators (including compound) must return T&.
A named, capture-less, non-generic lambda at namespace scope.
Overloads whose parameter list is a prefix of another overload.
By-reference captures of locals in a lambda that is returned or handed to a thread/async.
A [=] default capture together with this or a data member.
Redundant else after a branch that always jumps, and a function whose whole body is one if.
Interpreted as public *data* members: a class whose data members are all public (and nothing is private) should be a struct.
A struct with any private or protected member (data or function) is reported; the fix turns it into a class and keeps base-class access and the public section.
Reported for every const / reference data member unless all copy and move operations are deleted.
Counts user declarations (including = default / = delete) of the five special members; all or none.
Detects a constructor that allocates (new) into a raw-pointer member of a class that declares no destructor.
Stays silent for classes with base classes, because their copyability depends on the bases.
The fix moves the constants to default member initializers.
Constructors callable with one argument (including defaulted extras); copy/move and initializer_list constructors are on the positive list.
A class that introduces a virtual function must delete or hide (non-public) its copy operations.
Superseded by the C++20 rewritten comparison operators (member operator== is the C++20 idiom).
Applies to classes without base classes that introduce a virtual function; the fix adds a public virtual defaulted destructor.
Missing override is detected for base classes defined in the same file.
Reported only for classes whose every member function is virtual and has an implementation.
Reported for base classes defined in the same file when the derived class hides base overloads without a using-declaration.
Only the symmetric arithmetic/bitwise operators are checked; comparisons follow the C++20 rules.
All non-explicit conversion operators (including operator bool).
malloc/calloc/realloc/free and aligned_alloc.
new/delete outside resource-management functions; placement new is exempt.
More than one new/malloc in one statement.
[] parameters (main is exempt).
new assigned to a raw pointer (gsl::owner<T*> is accepted); the fix converts to std::make_unique.
For-statement initializers are reported but not auto-fixed.
Builtin types and pointers only (types with constructors are not reported); arrays (buffers) are not reported.
Detects an uninitialized declaration immediately followed by its first assignment.
Variable-length arrays and bounds that are not local constants.
Definitions of C-style variadic functions, <cstdarg> and va_* usage.
Bitwise operators mixed with other binary operators, and assignments that are not the leftmost operator.
Pointer arithmetic on pointer variables and non-constant indexing of C arrays / std::array declared in the same file.
Operands that modify and use the same variable (&&, || and ?: are sequenced and excluded).
A variable modified in one argument and used in another.
Numeric and character literals; the positive list is configurable (cpp20Guidelines.magicConstants.allowList). A literal that is the whole initializer of a variable counts as named.
Floating point to integral and long to char, for variables whose declared type is known.
NULL, and 0 used as a pointer in initializers, assignments, comparisons and returns.
reinterpret_cast is reported here; C-style and functional casts are reported through ES.49 / ES.64.
Resource-management functions are: constructors, destructors, operator new/delete, assignment operators, reset and release.
Slicing is reported for classes with data members that have derived classes in the same file.
Functional casts of builtin types (a class name cannot be told apart from a function without type information).
A chain of at least three branches comparing the same variable with literals.
Index loops over container[i] and begin()/end() iterator loops whose body only visits the elements.
The initializer/increment shares no identifier with the condition, or both are absent.
A case that falls through without break/return/throw/continue/goto, [[fallthrough]] or a noreturn call.
Enumerations defined in the same file; the fix adds the missing cases.
Comparisons with nullptr, true and false in conditions; integer comparisons with 0 are not redundant.
Declared signed vs unsigned variables, and signed variables against .size() / sizeof (ptrdiff_t is allowed, as the guideline says); the fix uses std::ssize.
Narrow definition: a function over builtin parameters whose only statement returns an expression of its parameters and literals.
std::thread is reported and std::jthread is proposed (C++20 prevails over gsl::joining_thread).
volatile variables and members.
Catching by value is reported for every class type, not only for types with a virtual function.
Uses a small table of the std::exception hierarchy plus classes defined in the same file.
Unconstrained type parameters of non-variadic templates and unconstrained auto parameters (also reports I.9); the quick fixes offer standard concepts.
typedef; simple typedefs are converted automatically.
Member types of class templates that do not use every template parameter.
size() compared with 0/1 and iterators compared with <.
Positive list from the guideline plus C++17 inline variables.
Includes after the first declaration (preprocessor directives and comments may precede them).
#pragma once is NOT accepted (the guideline says it is non-standard); the guard name is derived from the last two path components.
Only a quoted include of a standard header is detected; the filesystem is not consulted.
C arrays declared in a function or class that also declares an STL container.
<cstdio> and the printf family; simple printf/fprintf calls are converted to std::format.
Mixed tabs and spaces (reported once per file, with a whole-file fix) and block contents/closing braces not at the file's indentation step.
Reserved identifiers (double underscore, underscore + capital).
ALL_CAPS names that are not macros; single-letter template parameters are not names in this sense.
Names with camelCase humps. Types are Capitalized_with_underscores (e.g. My_map), everything else lower_case_with_underscores; a leading m_ or trailing _ on members is accepted.
Digit sequences with at least cpp20Guidelines.thresholds.digitSeparatorMinDigits digits (guideline: maybe 7).
No spaces inside <> of includes, before ; and , or [ , between a function name and ( , inside ( ) and [ ], and no runs of spaces between tokens (alignment before a trailing comment is tolerated).
public before protected before private, each once; types, then constructors/assignment/destructor, then functions, then data. The private section is exempt.

K&R/Stroustrup: function brace on its own line; class/struct and statement braces on the head's line; a space after if/for/while/switch/catch; branches and bodies on separate lines; case labels aligned with switch; types capitalized, functions not. A cuddled `} else {` is not checked (the guideline does not specify it).
T* p / T& r: the declarator operator attaches to the type.
Sibling statements or declarations sharing a line.
`T const` is reported; `const T` is the conventional notation.
Accepted suffixes are configurable: sources .cpp .cxx .cc .C, headers .h .hh .hpp .hxx.
